about: Every stretch of railway between neighbouring National Rail stations with any of it in England, from the OpenStreetMap United Kingdom extract of November 21st 2026 (download.openstreetmap.fr), made by build_stretches.py on 2026-11-22. A stretch is a pair of stations with no other station between them along the track, whether or not trains stop. id is the two codes in alphabetical order, a and b likewise; track runs from a to b ([longitude, latitude], simplified to within 5 metres). region is England's region with most of the stretch; crosses lists the other countries it runs into. operators are the train companies whose OpenStreetMap routes use at least half of it (incomplete). past, where present, names a station the stretch runs past: it may be an avoiding line that passenger trains don't use (see stretches-report.md).
